scope: A fixed deterministic 43-day, eight-aircraft two-base support configuration comparison: BASE-01 P-MAINT capacity one versus two, with every other input held fixed.
frozen_parent_observation: Parent BASE-01 PM aircraft 4 books the only maintainer at h24 through h25.
Two other BASE-01 aircraft request PM at h24.5 and initially fail the resource test; one books at h25 while another waits.
Parent's 2064 aggregate half-hour Resource bins have approximately 27.249758 queued resource-hours; its native log has 324 PM starts and 323 completions by h1032.
acceptance_hypotheses: Guarded session-0 SSH native import/export/calc/report completes with zero converter errors and no new warnings, exact authored-table roundtrip, nonempty output, preserved GUI PID13340 and raw SHA closure.

At the first BASE-01 PM wave, the added maintainer allows a second concurrent PM resource booking near h24.5, advancing at least one PM completion relative to the one-worker parent and reducing that local wait. Identify aircraft/resource events rather than assuming task IDs stay stable.

Across all 2064 half-hour bins, resource capacity, bookings, waiting, System state and Stock state reconcile with native events; mission request/outcome counts and terminal state are observed, not assumed.
The child remains failure-free with no item demand/backorder; the two-base 21-wave schedule remains fixed. Later PM event times may diverge because earlier maintenance completion changes the state.
limitations: This is one deterministic fixed-seed 43-day maintainer-capacity contrast, not a general staffing response or stochastic availability estimate.
Any later PM or mission timing changes are whole-model consequences and should not be attributed to a single local queue event.
Other resource classes, stock configurations, random failures, GUI visuals and cross-engine equivalence remain unverified.
